idea-plugin.name: Tailwind Rainbow
idea-plugin.description:
Colors Tailwind CSS variant prefixes so a long class list stays readable.

Every variant is painted in its own color, with related variants sharing one, so the structure of a class list is visible at a glance instead of having to be read word by word: hover, focus, sm, dark, container queries such as @md, attribute variants such as data-[state=open], arbitrary variants such as [&>*], and the ! important modifier wherever Tailwind allows it.

Where it reads class names. Class attributes and framework bindings (class, className, :class, v-bind:class, x-bind:class), class helper functions (cn, clsx, cva, twMerge, …), tagged templates including styled.div`…`, values assigned to a class-shaped name, and CSS @apply directives. Out of the box that covers HTML, JSX/TSX, Vue, Svelte, Astro, PHP and stylesheets - and the list of file types is a setting rather than a promise.

What you can change. Four themes ship: two decorative ones, a palette built on the Okabe-Ito colors so the variant families stay apart for color-blind readers, and one that takes its colors from your editor's own syntax scheme and follows it when you switch. Build your own on top of any of them - pick colors in the table, add variants no theme lists, switch entries off - or import a theme from the VS Code Tailwind Rainbow extension. Which attributes, helper functions and file types are scanned is configurable, and a project can keep its own answers and commit them. Colors that would not contrast with your editor background are adjusted until they do.

What it deliberately does not do. It does not sort, rewrite or complete class names, and it does not color utility classes out of the box: variants stop standing out once everything else is colored too, so base-class coloring is something you opt into.

Everything lives under Settings | Editor | Tailwind Rainbow.
